pr.title: Stop a test chunk that hangs instead of waiting on it forever
pr.head: f865dd87d954f6671a0074f259dd5b629a854aee

summary: python3 -m tests is Projector's test runner. It splits the suite into chunks, lists of at most eight tests from one class, and runs each chunk as its own python3 -m unittest process, several at a time.

Before this change, each chunk inherited the runner's stdin, and the runner waited on each chunk with no time limit. Started from a background shell, whose stdin never closes, one test's fake claude script piped its input through cat, and cat waited forever, so the whole run did too. At a terminal or in CI, stdin closes or is empty, so the hang never showed there.

• No stdin. Each chunk starts with stdin connected to /dev/null, so a test that reads stdin reads nothing and goes on.
  • A time limit. Each chunk runs in a process group of its own. Past --timeout seconds, 300 by default, the runner kills the whole group and fails the chunk with The chunk ran past 300 seconds and was stopped.

The runner kills the group rather than the chunk's process alone because a process a test started, such as that cat, holds the chunk's output pipes open, and the runner would keep waiting to read them.

groups.title: The runner stops a chunk that hangs
groups.kicker: No stdin for a chunk, and a timeout that kills its whole process group
intro: run starts one chunk. It replaces subprocess.run with a Popen so that on a timeout it can kill the chunk's process group before reading the rest of the output. A process group is the set of processes the chunk and everything it starts belong to; start_new_session=True gives the chunk a group of its own, so os.killpg reaches its children without touching the runner.
The tests in tests/test_runner.py drive run directly with a small probe module written to a temporary directory: one probe test pipes stdin through cat, and another waits on a sleep 60 child.

checks.text: The new tests and the pull request's reproduction pass at this head: tests.test_runner printed OK in about 1 second, and tests.test_ci.ActionTests with a stdin held open by sleep 120 printed OK in about 1 second. The check CI job passed too.

files.note: The runner: run starts each chunk with no stdin and a timeout, and --timeout sets the limit.

checks.text: communicate raised TimeoutExpired before it reaped the chunk, so the group still exists when killpg runs, and the second communicate returns once every process holding the pipes is dead.

os.killpg exists only on POSIX. On Windows a chunk that times out raises AttributeError here, and the with block then waits on the hung chunk, which is how the runner behaved before this change. The review suggests falling back to process.kill().

files.note: Two tests of run: a chunk ignores a stdin that never closes, and a chunk past its timeout fails along with its children.

checks.text: The comment above the stdin test tells the hang's history in the past tense ("waited on cat for hours") rather than the reason in the present tense, which guidelines.md § 1 and writing.md § 12 ask for. The review keeps this open as a P2 finding.
